message:
You’re absolutely right: we can (and should) be candid about real delivery impact while staying strictly focused on post-return behaviors and avoiding any reference to protected leave. I’ve already updated the review to make the urgency and timeline impact clearer by:
- Executive summary: Added schedule pressure and the need for faster feedback cycles, tighter WIP, and daily risk calls.
- New section: “Team impact and timelines (post-return observations)” that describes how latency and context gaps affect dependent work and forecasting, with mitigation steps.

If you’d like, I can strengthen it further with more specific, measurable phrasing. Below are suggested rewrites you can approve (I’ll apply them once you confirm and/or provide numbers):

Proposed wording upgrades (pick and choose)
- Executive summary (stronger impact framing)
  - The crawler roadmap is at risk if review and status latency exceed 1 business day. To protect Q commitments, Emily’s ramp needs accelerated feedback loops, smaller batch sizes, and explicit daily risk calls.

- Team impact and timelines (add quantification)
  - In the last [N] weeks, we observed slippage on [X/Y] dependent tasks when status or review response time exceeded 1 business day, increasing rework and batching.
  - Context gaps in [module A/B] added [~Z hours] of pairing per ticket and elongated cycle time, reducing predictability in sprint forecasts.
  - Mitigation in place: daily risk calls, smaller PRs (<[lines or scope]), and pairing on high-impact paths until review latency and cycle time improve.

- Areas to focus (more measurable targets)
  - Communication: Post a daily status and risk call by [time] with blockers explicitly tagged. Aim to escalate risks same-day to EM/PM when scope or sequence changes.
  - Review responsiveness: Respond to review requests within 1 business day; keep PRs < [300] LOC where feasible to reduce latency.
  - Throughput: Target [4–6] PRs/week with smaller batch sizes; close [2–3] medium tickets end-to-end per sprint.
  - Context acceleration: Pair on [module A/B] [2–3] times per week until independent ownership is reached; time-box deep dives to [90 minutes] with clear outcomes.
  - Documentation: Convert new context into concise runbooks; produce [2] updates this quarter to reduce repeat questions.

- Commitments and risk management (explicit guardrails)
  - If a milestone is at risk, propose a replan (de-scope, sequence change, or pairing) within 24 hours.
  - Weekly milestone review with EM/PM to validate scope and confirm next week’s deliverables.
  - Track PR cadence, review latency, and cycle time in a lightweight dashboard to make progress visible.

What I need from you to finalize
- Optional: concrete numbers for the placeholders (e.g., “X/Y tasks slipped,” average review latency, typical PR sizes, specific modules).
- Whether you want me to apply these rewrites directly to /workspace/peer_review_emily.md now.
- Any org-specific language or rating scales to align with your PeopleOps template.

Once you confirm, I’ll update the file with the selected phrasing and metrics, keeping it candid, specific, and compliant.
